lines.en: Good morning, Pia! **How was your weekend?**
lines.pt: Bom dia, Pia! Como foi o seu fim de semana?

lines.en: Pretty good, thanks! I went hiking. And you?
lines.pt: Muito bom, obrigada! Fui fazer trilha. E você?

lines.en: Yes, with my sister. It was sunny.
lines.pt: Sim, com a minha irmã. Fez sol.

lines.en: Great weather! Mine was quiet. I watched a movie.
lines.pt: Que tempo ótimo! O meu foi tranquilo. Assisti a um filme.

lines.en: Yes, please. **Are you busy** this afternoon?
lines.pt: Sim, por favor. Você está ocupada esta tarde?

lines.en: Want to have lunch together later?

pages.title: Workplace small talk

situation.text: It is Monday morning at your new office in the United States. You meet a coworker at the coffee machine and have a short, friendly chat.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can start a friendly chat at work, ask about the weekend, ask a simple follow-up question and invite someone for lunch.
canDo: Start a chat: How was your weekend?
success: I end the chat in a friendly way.
pages.think: What do you talk about with coworkers in Portuguese? Are those topics “safe” everywhere?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação real: o café da manhã de segunda-feira no escritório.
solo: Pergunte sobre o que o estudante conversa no intervalo do trabalho.
Mostre os 4 critérios.
group: Cada estudante diz um assunto típico de intervalo.
extra: Do you like your coworkers?
What do you usually drink at work?
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about weekends and work.
intro.group: One question per student, then a question back to a classmate.

pages.recall: At the library (last lesson): “Can I borrow…?”. Ask: Can I borrow your pen?

qs.q: What did you do last weekend?
qs.pt: O que você fez no fim de semana passado?

qs.q: What is your favorite weekend activity?
qs.pt: Qual é a sua atividade favorita no fim de semana?

pages.tip: Use the answers to practice simple past: stayed, saw, worked.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma e ativar o passado simples de verbos comuns.
extra: Where did you go?
Who did you go with?

errors.w: I go to the beach yesterday.
errors.r: I went to the beach yesterday.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Small talk is part of the work day in the United States. Look at the cards and guess before you read.

cards.note: Short, friendly talks near the coffee machine or in the kitchen.
Weather, weekend, food, hobbies, travel and sports.
With new people: salary, age, politics, religion.

qs.q: What do coworkers talk about in small talk?
qs.pt: Sobre o que os colegas conversam?

levels.A2: They talk about the weekend, food or plans.
levels.B1: Typical topics are the weekend, the weather, food, hobbies and travel.
levels.B2: Light topics such as the weekend, sports or travel help people connect without getting too personal.

qs.q: Is “How are you?” a real question?
qs.pt: “How are you?” é uma pergunta de verdade?

levels.A2: Often it is a greeting. You say “Good, thanks!”
levels.B1: It is usually a greeting, so a short answer like “Good, thanks. You?” is enough.
levels.B2: Usually it works as a greeting, not as a request for details, unless you know the person well.

qs.q: How do you end a short chat?

levels.A2: I say: “Nice talking to you. See you later!”
levels.B1: I say something friendly and mention work: “I should get back to it. Talk later!”
levels.B2: I wrap up politely, for example “Good to catch up; I’d better get back to work.”

pages.compare: In Brazil people may ask more personal questions early on (family, age, salary can come up). In the US small talk often stays lighter at first. What is normal where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto: temas seguros e pergunta-cumprimento.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses.
Compare com o ambiente de trabalho do estudante.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica.
answers: Q3: friendly closing and back to work.
extra: What topic is too personal for you?
What do people talk about in your office?
support: Use as respostas A1 como andaime.
stretch: B2: discuta como as normas variam por região e empresa; evite generalizações absolutas.

pass1.q: What are Raj and Pia doing?
pass1.pt: O que Raj e Pia estão fazendo?

teach.goal: Compreender o essencial antes de ver o texto.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: o que fazem.
2ª escuta: atividade, com quem, filme e hora do almoço.
extra: Who is more talkative?
How do they feel about the weekend?

qs.q: What did Pia do on the weekend?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê o Raj; você lê a Pia.
Peça que reconte.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
answers: She went hiking · he watched a movie · coffee · at noon
extra: What did YOU do last weekend?
Is this chat formal?
support: Mostre o PT depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.pt: Como foi o seu fim de semana?
items.use: Start small talk, especially on Monday.
items.alt: Also: **Did you have a good weekend?**

items.use: Ask a follow-up about the past: Did you go out?
Check if the person has time: Are you busy now?
React to good news or plans. Also: Sounds relaxing / fun.
Give the turn back after your answer.

items.alt: More polite: **Would you like some coffee?**

items.use: A short answer to “What did you do?”

pages.note: Choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks e descobrir a função.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?”.
Peça um exemplo próprio.
group: Cada estudante escolhe uma ★ e explica.
answers: Starting a chat · Follow-up · Reacting · Checking time · Giving the turn back
extra: Which one is for a friend and which for a boss?

errors.w: How was the weekend of you?

patterns.name: Checking availability
patterns.formula: **Are you busy** + now / today / after lunch?

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: I hope you had a pleasant weekend.
Would you care for some coffee?
register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules.

teach.goal: Fixar 2 padrões (How was…? / Did you…?). Did + verbo base.
solo: Mostre o padrão no diálogo.
Use “Swap the words”.
teach.answers: Padrões 01/02 são o foco; 03/04 são expansão.
extra: Ask a different follow-up question.
Answer with a past verb.
support: Só How was your weekend? e a resposta I went… na 1ª rodada.
stretch: Combine: How was your trip? Did you see anything famous?

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In fast speech, did you sounds like “didja” and want to sounds like “wanna”. You do not have to say them this way, but you should understand them.

own.prompt: Write one question with “Did you…?” and one with “Want to…?” for a coworker.
own.criteria: Say each one twice: slowly, then reduced. Does your partner understand both?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: reduções (did you → didja, want to → wanna).
solo: Modele devagar e rápido.
Identify e depois uso próprio.
answers: Identify 1: Did you go? · Identify 2: Want to have lunch?

errors.w: Did you com “d-i-d-y-o-u” separado e lento sempre
Want to com “t” duro e pausa

support: Foque em reconhecer (escuta); só depois em produzir.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. It is Monday. You start small talk.
2. Your coworker says “I went hiking.” Ask a follow-up.
3. Your coworker says “I watched a great movie.”
4. You want to invite someone for lunch. Check first.

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.instr: Make it a question about the past:

items.why: Answer and give the turn back.

items.q: You are free. Choose the best reply.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça duas versões.
answers: 1: How was your weekend? · 2: Did you go with friends? · 3: Sounds nice! · 4: Are you busy at noon?
Gap: was · go · Did you go out? · How was your trip? · Pretty good, thanks! And you? · Not really. Why?
extra: Say each answer naturally, with a smile.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — chat at the coffee machine

brief.teacher: You are a coworker. Ask about the weekend and give short answers to test the student.
brief.student: You are a new employee: start a chat, ask a follow-up and invite the coworker to lunch.

orders: Greet and ask about the weekend
Ask a follow-up with Did you…?
Invite to lunch (check Are you busy…?)
complications: The coworker only says “Fine.” Ask another question.
You do not know a word: ask for help.
Someone asks a personal question: change the topic politely.
success: I end the chat in a friendly way.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Use o fim de semana real do estudante.
Rodada 1: chunks. Rodada 2: palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções.
extra: What do you say when you are very busy?
stretch: Mude de assunto com naturalidade: “By the way…”.

rounds.task: Ask your partner about the weekend.

rounds.title: Follow-up

rounds.title: React and invite
rounds.task: React and invite your partner for lunch or coffee.

a.title: Student A
a.task: You know two weekend activities. Ask about the rest.

b.title: Student B
b.task: You know two weekend activities. Ask about the rest.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição com informações novas.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada.
Cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
answers: A: soccer; sleep late. B: dinner with friends; watch a movie.
extra: What do you do on Saturday night?
Do you like Sundays?

pages.title: Group mission — the coffee-machine chat
pages.goal: Each group must keep a friendly work chat going for two minutes and end it politely.

missions.mission: Start small talk on Monday. Ask about the weekend and give a full answer.
missions.constraint: Use “How was your weekend?” and “Did you…?”

missions.mission: One person is busy. Check availability and agree on a time to talk.
Plan a team lunch. Ask about each person’s weekend first.
missions.constraint: Each person asks one question and gives one answer.

success: End the chat in a friendly way.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: manter uma conversa leve.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão.
Progressão: com apoio → palavras-chave → sem roteiro.
answers: Modelo: “How was your weekend?” → “Good! I went hiking. And you?” → “Sounds nice! Did you…?”
extra: How do you end a chat politely?
support: Dê o início de frase em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short chat message to a coworker. Ask about the weekend and invite the person to coffee.
pages.model: Hi Pia! **How was your weekend?** I stayed home and watched a movie. **Are you busy** at 3 p.m.? Want to get a coffee? Let me know!
checklist: I closed in a friendly way.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos.
group: Troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add one sentence about your weekend.

errors.r: Do you want a coffee? / Want to get a coffee?

support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You asked a follow-up and reacted to the answer.
prompts.improve: Example: Use did + base verb: Did you go?
prompts.next: Example: Keep a two-minute chat going without notes.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

tasks.name: Build a question
tasks.prompt: Without notes: ask a coworker about the weekend.

tasks.name: Respond to a situation
tasks.prompt: A coworker says: “I went to the beach.” React.

tasks.name: Use a new expression
tasks.prompt: Check if someone is free this afternoon.

items: Record a 45-second audio: tell what you did last weekend.
Write three follow-up questions with Did you…?
Practice didja / wanna by listening to a short video.
Listen to the dialogue again and underline two expressions.

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem anotações: pergunta, resposta e expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; combine a tarefa.
answers: How was your weekend? · Sounds nice! · Are you busy this afternoon?
extra: Revisão espaçada: próxima aula, uma semana e missão da unidade.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.goal: Start with words and a smile.

ladder.say: How was your weekend? Did you go out?
How was your weekend? I stayed home, but I heard you went hiking.
ladder.goal: Share and ask about a detail.

ladder.say: I’ve been meaning to ask how your trip went, since you mentioned it last week.
I hope you managed to get some rest over the weekend; it sounded like a hectic few days.
I trust the weekend afforded you some well-earned respite after such a demanding week.
ladder.goal: Use a polished register with warmth.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
